the effects of diet on plasma lipids, lipoproteins, and apolipoproteins.
the mechanisms by which dietary carbohydrates affect plasma triacylglyerol metabolism in NIDDM.

the increased plasma triacylglyerol concentration with the high-carbohydrate, low-fat diet in NIDDM is due to the increased hepatic secretion and not to decreased lipoprotein lipolytic clearance.

high-carbohydrate, low-fat diets are associated with increased hepatic secretion rates of very-low-density lipoprotein triacylgycerols and that the increase in fasting plasma triacylglcerol concentrations is not related to reduced postprandial lipoprotein clearance or increased lipolysis.
